To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the value of a firm is positively associated with foreign currency hedging, 2) foreign currency hedging increases a firm’s value through the tax shield effect and the expected financial distress costs effect, 3) the value of foreign currency hedging decreases when the firm’s debt level is high, and 4) foreign currency hedgings have a stronger effect on firm value when firms’ foreign sales are high. 2.1.1 Theoretical Background.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of foreign currency hedging on firm value.
the question of whether foreign currency hedging affects firm value.
the effect of foreign currency hedging on the value of firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a positive relationship between hedging and firm value.
the effect of hedgng on firm value depends on the nature of the risk and the hedging instruments used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of hedgers on value is positive and statistically significant.
the use of derivatives can increase firm value, and that the effect is more pronounced when firms use more derivatives and when the derivatives are more complex.
hedging can affect a firm’s value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hedging is not a one size fits all strategy.
the value of hedging is highly sensitive to the hedging strategy employed by a firm.
the effect of hedged foreign currency exposure is positive and significant, but that it varies across different industries and countries.
